title: Replicating Homogeneity on Cybersecurity Domain Tasks

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling and critical: shared blind spots in cybersecurity AI can be actively weaponized by adversaries. This is not just a passive risk but an exploitable vulnerability affecting critical infrastructure.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing valid cybersecurity reasoning prompts requires domain expertise. CVE analysis and vulnerability identification are specialized. CS students may lack the security background needed.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: construct prompt set, run through models, compute similarity. The prompt construction is the main effort; analysis pipeline is reusable from prior work.

novelty.reasoning: No published work has applied the Artificial Hivemind homogeneity methodology specifically to cybersecurity reasoning tasks. Existing cybersecurity LLM research focuses on vulnerabilities of LLMs themselves (prompt injection, etc.) or their use in CTI, but not on whether multiple models produce homogeneous security assessments. This is a novel and high-impact intersection.

evidence.finding: Measures homogeneity on general open-ended queries but does not focus on cybersecurity-specific tasks.

evidence.source: Uncovering Vulnerabilities of LLM-Assisted Cyber Threat Intelligence (2025)
evidence.finding: Identifies three fundamental failure modes in LLMs for CTI (spurious correlations, contradictory knowledge, constrained generalization) but does not measure inter-model homogeneity.
82.4% of models can be compromised through inter-agent trust exploitation, showing shared vulnerabilities but not measuring output homogeneity on security reasoning tasks.
